creatures.name: Hollow Thrall
creatures.description: A villager three days dead and still wearing their own boots. The eyes are gone and the sockets are packed with grave soil.
specials: Cannot be commanded away from the tether that raised it.
Takes no action of its own if the Avatar falls.

taunts: The thrall leans in close, its jaw working without a sound.
hurt: The thrall looks down at the wound as if it belonged to someone else.
dying: The thrall sits down in the leaves, carefully, and is still.

creatures.name: The Hollow Avatar
creatures.description: A standing absence in the shape of a tall man, wearing the grove's shadows like a coat. Where it has walked, the ground has not sprung back.

attacks.name: unmaking touch
attacks.on_critical: The target's most recent memory of daylight goes out.

specials: Draws one Hollow Thrall upright again at the start of each round while any remain standing.
Cannot leave the Hollow Grove while the turned earth at its centre is undisturbed.

taunts: Cold, isn't it? It gets colder.
I will keep you. I keep everything.
hurt: You... take from me? From ME?
dying: Tell him... tell him I kept them... for him...

creatures.name: Crimson Covenant Acolyte
creatures.description: A well-fed young person in good boots and a borrowed cloak, holding a knife they have clearly been taught to hold and never taught to use.
specials: Flees the chamber if Malachai falls, and is not pursued.

taunts: For the Vessel!
You see? You see what faith can do?
hurt: This was not in the catechism.
dying: I was promised... I was promised...

creatures.name: Malachai Vex
creatures.description: Still aristocratic, still unhurried, and no longer entirely occupying his own outline. The shadow behind him moves a half-beat before he does.

attacks.name: entropy lance
attacks.on_critical: The ritual circles brighten. Something below the floor answers.

specials: While the ritual circles are intact, damage that would drop him instead leaves him at 1 Hit Point once per fight.
Speaks throughout, and will stop to answer a genuine question.

taunts: Did that hurt? It will stop. Everything stops.
Such a small life, and so much of it on the floor.
hurt: Interesting. Truly. Do that again.
dying: You have... only... postponed... it...

creatures.name: Covenant Cutthroat
creatures.description: A Millhaven face you half recognise from the market, with a cudgel in one hand and a length of red cord tied round the other wrist. Paid, and not paid enough to look you in the eye.
specials: Breaks and runs at the first real wound once the others are down.

taunts: Should have stayed in the Sparrow.
Nothing personal. It's paid.
hurt: Not paid enough for this. Not near enough.
dying: Tell Wendel... tell him he still owes me...

creatures.name: Mere-Drowned
creatures.description: Something that went into the mere a long time ago with a rope round its ankles and a stone on the rope, and has come back up with both. It is not one of the Avatar's. Somebody else asked it up.
specials: Drags whatever it holds toward the water's edge instead of striking it again.

taunts: The drowned thing drags you toward the water's edge.
hurt: Black water pours from the wound, and keeps pouring.
dying: It goes back into the mere, and the stone on its rope pulls it down.

creatures.name: Archive Warden
creatures.description: A suit of palace armour with nobody in it, walking a patrol it was given before the library had its present name. There is a key in its back, and the key is turning.
specials: Stops mid-swing if the key in its back is drawn out. Nobody can reach it from the front.

taunts: The warden's halberd comes round on its patrol, and you are in the way.
hurt: Something inside the warden's armour grinds and slips a gear.
dying: The key in its back stops turning.

creatures.name: Ossuary Reader
creatures.description: It was an archivist once, by the ink still in the creases of its knuckles. It has been kept down here to guard the stair, and fed just enough, and it is hungry now in a way that has nothing to do with reading.
specials: Its claws numb; whatever they open finds its hands slow to answer.

taunts: Quiet. Quiet. Quiet.
Mmm. Fresh margins.
hurt: Hurts. Hurts like paper cuts.
dying: Shelve me... shelve me... in the... right... place...

creatures.name: The Ravencrest Scarecrow
creatures.description: Marta's scarecrow, down off its pole and three fields from where it was put: a turnip head gone soft, a coat that was her father's, and a child's ribbon round one wrist. It stands with its arms out, as though it were still keeping birds off something.
specials: Burns. It has stood in the rain for years, and it burns anyway.

taunts: The scarecrow swings its stuffed arms, and there is something hard inside the straw.
hurt: Straw bursts out of the coat, and it does not seem to notice.
dying: The scarecrow falls back into its crucifix stretch and topples over, stiff as a post.

creatures.name: Red-Veined Miner
creatures.description: Nine went down on the last shift. What is left of them is still down here, still working, with the red grain of the stone grown up through their arms like ivy up a wall. They do not stop swinging when you speak to them.
specials: Keeps the rhythm of a working shift, and strikes on the beat.

taunts: The miner's pick comes down on the beat, and you are the face.
hurt: Red light bleeds from the miner instead of blood.
dying: The miner stops mid-swing, and the red goes out of its eyes.

creatures.name: Thornhaven Gate-Warden
creatures.description: Malachai's household guard, in red-lacquered plate with the Vex crest filed off, and a halberd each. They are guarding the gatehouse from the outside, and its door from the inside, which tells you what it is for.
specials: Holds the gatehouse door rather than give chase.

taunts: Back from the door.
Vex pays for every one of you we drop.
hurt: Hold. Hold, damn it.
dying: Should have... walked away... myself...

creatures.name: Crimson Zealot
creatures.description: The last of the Covenant's faithful, who followed the Queen down when the rest ran. They have cut the crimson out of their coats and bound it round their wrists instead, tight enough to hurt.
specials: Fights to the end. There is nothing left above for it to go back to.

taunts: For the Queen, and for what comes after her!
You should have stayed up in the light.
hurt: The Queen will remember this.
dying: Tell her... I held the stair...

creatures.name: The Unmade
creatures.description: Somebody of the Quiet Kingdom who chose, with the rest, to stop, and did not quite manage it. There is less of them than there should be, and the edges are soft, like a word rubbed out.
specials: Wherever it touches, cloth frays and iron rusts.

taunts: The Unmade lays a hand on you, and your sleeve comes unravelled where it touched.
hurt: The wound closes the wrong way, and there is a little less of it.
dying: It stops, all at once, and is not there.

creatures.name: Hierophant of the Unmaking
creatures.description: The priest who led the Quiet Kingdom in its last prayer, kept on its feet by the unfinished end of it. Its vestments have faded to no colour at all. Its voice has not.
specials: Every line of the litany it finishes takes something from the room: a colour, a sound, a name.

taunts: And the lamp was put out, and it was good.
Every line brings us closer to the last.
hurt: I have lost my place. No matter.
dying: At... last... the... end...

creatures.name: Rift-Maw
creatures.description: Something that lived in the rock under the capital and never needed to come up, until the rock split. It is mostly mouth, and the mouth is mostly stone.
specials: Swallows what it kills whole, armour and all.

taunts: The maw heaves up out of the floor and closes on you with a noise like a quarry.
hurt: Stone flakes off the maw's jaws in sheets.
dying: The maw sinks into the floor and grinds, slower and slower, to a stop.

creatures.name: The Name-Eater
creatures.description: The Quiet Kingdom's last servant, made to take every name off the causeway once its people were gone, so there would be nobody left to remember. It has been at the work a thousand years. It has got used to the taste.

attacks.name: unwriting tongue
attacks.on_critical: For a moment nobody in the party can remember your name.

specials: Speaks only in names it has eaten. It has eaten a great many.

taunts: Thorne. Harrow. Brask. Mercy.
Yours next. Say it for me.
hurt: Pell. Pell. Pell.
dying: No... names... left...

creatures.name: The Last Quiet King
creatures.description: His crown went up out of here long ago, to be traded from hand to hand in the kingdom above. When his people chose to stop he stayed to see it done, and it was never quite done. He is very tired, and very courteous, and he would like you to stop too.
specials: Asks each of you, before he fights you, whether you would like to stop. He means it kindly.

taunts: Would you like to stop? You may.
There is no shame in being tired.
hurt: Ah. I had forgotten this.
dying: Thank you. I could not... finish it... myself...

creatures.name: Quiet Courtier
creatures.description: A courtier still in its place at the side of the approach, in robes gone the grey of old paper, with a thin blade it never draws until the King has finished speaking.
specials: Never raises its voice. Never needs to.

taunts: The courtier's blade finds the gap in your guard without a sound.
hurt: The courtier inclines its head at the wound, politely.
dying: The courtier folds down into its robes and is still.

creatures.name: Last Seal-Breaker
creatures.description: One of the Covenant's masons, who spent a life learning where a seal will crack, and has come down to the last of them with a chisel and a mallet and the patience of a stone-cutter.
specials: Stops working the seal only long enough to kill you, and goes straight back to it after.

taunts: Every seal cracks. You only have to know where.
You are standing in my light.
hurt: That is my chisel hand!
dying: It was... cracking... I heard it...

creatures.name: The Shadow Vessel
creatures.description: What the Quiet Kingdom made to end itself, and then, at the last, chose not to use. It is not awake. It is dreaming, and what it dreams of is everything being still.

attacks.name: the long dark
attacks.on_critical: The light goes out of the world for a moment, and does not come back all the way.

specials: It fights like something dreaming, and every wound it takes wakes it a little more.

taunts: The Vessel reaches out in its sleep, and where it touches, the world goes thin.
hurt: The Vessel stirs at the wound, and the dark in the Cradle deepens.
dying: The Vessel sighs, a long sigh like the tide going out, and is still.

creatures.name: Liora, Vessel-Bound
creatures.description: The Queen of Valorheim, on her knees in the Cradle with the Vessel's chain wound round both wrists. She has not come down here to wake it. She has come down to wear it.
specials: Where she bleeds, the Vessel does.

taunts: Kneel. I am still your Queen, for a little while longer.
You were always going to lose. I read the ending first.
hurt: You would cut me? Your Queen?
dying: Aldric... tell him... I was nearly... something...

creatures.name: Copper-Tongue Rat
creatures.description: A rat the size of a terrier with a green stain round its muzzle, the colour a penny goes. They follow coin. Nobody in Millhaven can tell you how they know where it is.
specials: Goes for the purse, not the throat, until something stands in the way.

taunts: The rat gets its teeth into your belt pouch and worries it.
hurt: The rat squeals, and three more squeals answer from the ditch.
dying: The rat drops, with a copper penny still in its teeth.

creatures.name: Hedge Footpad
creatures.description: Somebody who was in the Sparrow when you paid for your drinks, and a sister-in-law's hatchet, and a scarf over the face that fools nobody.
specials: Runs the moment it is clear the money is not coming quietly.

taunts: Purses. Now.
I did say nobody needed to be brave.
hurt: This was meant to be easy!
dying: My sister-in-law... wants her hatchet back...

creatures.name: Covenant Tithe-Taker
creatures.description: The Covenant keeps an account of what everybody has. This one carries the page with your names on it, and a knife for crossing a name out.
specials: Reads out the sum you are worth before it starts, and gets it right to the copper.

taunts: Tithe paid in part.
The Covenant is patient. I am not.
hurt: You will be charged for that.
dying: The account... is not... closed...

creatures.name: Gilt Harpy
creatures.description: Feathers the colour of old brass, and a woman's face that has never had to smile at anyone. She lines her nest with rings, and with the fingers that were in them.
specials: Sings when she is winning. Stop the song and she stops being sure of herself.

taunts: Pretty rings. Pretty fingers.
Sing with me! Sing!
hurt: My feathers! You will pay in gold for my feathers!
dying: My nest... my shining nest...

creatures.name: Hoard-Wight
creatures.description: He was buried with his money on the understanding that it would stay with him. It did not. He has been walking the valley ever since, following gold he hopes is his.

attacks.name: grave-cold grip
attacks.on_critical: A coin in your purse goes black and will not come clean.

specials: Stops to count any coin that is thrown down, and counts slowly.

taunts: Mine.
Mine. Mine. Mine.
hurt: You cannot take it with you. I tried.
dying: Was it... ever... mine...

creatures.name: Ash Ogre
creatures.description: Nine feet of ogre gone grey from the fall of ash off the mines, carrying a club that was a pit prop and a sack that is already half full of other people's valuables.
specials: Wants the sack filled more than it wants you dead, and will take a bribe that is big enough.

taunts: In the sack you go!
Shiny things for the sack!
hurt: Ow! Ow! Not the sack!
dying: Sack... was... nearly... full...

creatures.name: Cinder Drake
creatures.description: A drake can smell gold the way a hound smells meat, and this one has smelled yours from the other side of the valley. Its scales shed sparks when it breathes.
specials: Will not leave while it can smell the gold; will not stay once the gold is out of reach.

taunts: The drake snaps, and sparks shower off its teeth.
hurt: The drake hisses, and the air around the wound shimmers with heat.
dying: The drake's fire goes out, and it cools to ash in front of you.

creatures.name: Red-Vein Stalker
creatures.description: Bloodstone ore given legs and a single instruction by somebody in the Covenant. The instruction was your names. The red grain in it pulses when it is near what it wants.
specials: Does not tire, does not sleep, and does not stop walking toward you until it is broken.

taunts: The stalker's fist comes down like a hammer on an anvil.
hurt: A crack runs through the stalker, and the red light in it flickers.
dying: The stalker comes apart into ore, and the red goes out of it.

creatures.name: Crimson Inquisitor
creatures.description: A woman in a red coat and a clerk's spectacles who has read your names in a ledger with a very large sum written next to them, and who does not like sums that stay large.

attacks.name: word of the Vessel
attacks.on_critical: For a moment you cannot remember what you were carrying.

specials: Will talk, if you ask what she wants. What she wants is everything.

taunts: Recorded.
You are worth less already.
hurt: That will be entered in the ledger against you.
dying: Balance... carried... forward...

creatures.name: The Tithe-Knight
creatures.description: An armoured revenant who collected the Crown's taxes three hundred years ago, and who has never been told to stop. Its writ is still nailed to its breastplate.
specials: Accepts payment in full. Nobody has ever had enough.

taunts: Monies owed.
The Crown will be paid.
hurt: Obstruction of a collector. Noted.
dying: Account... settled...

creatures.name: Hound of the Vessel
creatures.description: Something the Shadow Vessel has let off its leash. It has the outline of a hound and the manners of a debt collector, and everywhere it has walked the gold has gone dull.
specials: Tarnishes gold it touches. What it takes, it takes for the Vessel, not for itself.

taunts: The hound's bite leaves no mark, and the gold at your belt goes dull.
hurt: The hound flickers, like a shadow when a lamp gutters.
dying: The hound lies down, and there is only a shadow on the ground, and then not even that.

creatures.name: The Hoardmother
creatures.description: Old enough to remember when Valorheim paid her tribute, and offended that it stopped. She has heard what you are worth. She considers it hers.

attacks.name: breath of the hoard
attacks.on_critical: Whatever gold you carried is a puddle.

specials: Talks before she fights, and means every word of it.

taunts: Tribute. At last.
Kneel, and I may leave you your teeth.
hurt: You scratched me. Nobody has scratched me in four hundred years.
dying: Valorheim... owes me... still...

encounters.name: Something Keeping Pace
encounters.description: The thing that has been matching your steps stops pretending to.

scene.setting: A week ago these were Millhaven people: a drover, a farmhand, somebody who kept bees. Whatever raised them walked them out into the wood and left them to keep it.
ambiance: Leaves come down in the still air, a few at a time.
Somewhere behind you, a third set of footsteps starts, and stops.
The thralls make no sound at all, not even breathing.

opening.text: The nearer one turns its head toward you the way a sleeper turns toward a voice. Its boots are still laced.

opening.pc: Whoever you were, I am sorry. Stay down this time.

first_down.pc: That one had a name. Remember it was somebody.

victory.text: They lie in the leaves as if they had only sat down to rest.

victory.pc: Aldus will want to know. He will want their names.

defeat.text: The last thing you see is a pair of good boots, standing patiently by your head, waiting for instructions.

flee.text: They do not follow past the nails. Not yet.

encounters.name: The Hollow Avatar
encounters.description: The turned earth at the centre of the clearing shifts, and the thing that has been wearing Millhaven's dead stands up out of it.

scene.setting: The heart of it. Elara is somewhere under that turned earth, kept, and the thing standing over the grave has been waiting for somebody to come for her.
ambiance: The trees lean in a little further, as if to watch.
The turned earth in the centre heaves once, like breath.
Every shadow in the clearing points toward the Avatar, whatever the light says.

opening.enemy: You are not the one I kept her for. Still. You will do to begin with.

opening.pc: She is going home. Stand aside or be put aside.

opening.enemy: Home. I remember home. It was cold there too.

bloodied.pc: It can be hurt. Keep on it!

first_down.pc: One less of its puppets. The strings are next.

victory.text: The shadows in the clearing let go of the Avatar all at once, and there is nothing inside them.
Under the turned earth, very faintly, a child is crying.

victory.pc: Dig. Carefully. She is alive.

defeat.enemy: Lie down with the others. I will keep you too.

flee.enemy: Run, then. The wood is mine to the nails, and the nails are coming out.

encounters.name: Prevent the Ascension
encounters.description: He closes the ledger, sets it down with care, and stands. The two acolytes move to the edges of the circle without being told.

scene.setting: The top of Thornhaven, with the city burning below the windows. Every circle on the floor is drawn to open something, and Malachai has been drawing them for years.
ambiance: The circles on the floor brighten, dim, brighten, like a pulse.
Below the windows the city burns without a sound reaching up here.
Something under the floor answers every word Malachai says.

opening.enemy: Ah. The farmers' friends. You broke the geode; I felt it. You have no idea what you let out doing it.

opening.pc: Then tell us, Vex. You like talking.

opening.enemy: I do. I shall talk the whole time I am killing you.

bloodied.pc: He bleeds like anyone. Keep him off the circles!

first_down.enemy: Acolytes are cheap. Faith is not. Do not flatter yourselves.

victory.text: The circles go out one ring at a time, from the outside in, and the thing under the floor stops answering.

victory.pc: It is over. It is actually over.

defeat.enemy: Lie still. You will want to be facing the right way when it opens.

flee.enemy: Go. Tell them what you saw. Fear makes such a good congregation.

encounters.name: Paid to Wait
encounters.description: Two figures stand up out of the reeds on either side of the causeway with cudgels already in hand. Neither of them looks surprised to see you.
encounters.rearm_description: There are two more of them on the causeway now, standing exactly where the first two stood, red cord at their wrists. They have been waiting for you to come back up this road. They knew you would.

scene.setting: The Mere Road was never a road anyone used. Somebody wanted you on it anyway, and paid these two to be waiting when you came.
ambiance: The black water on either side of the causeway does not move.
A bell rings once, far out on the mere, for nobody.
Reeds hiss in a wind you cannot feel.

opening.enemy: Wendel said you'd be along. Said you'd have a look about you. You do.

opening.pc: Wendel said a lot of things. How much did he get for us?

opening.enemy: More than you'll be worth by teatime.

bloodied.enemy: This isn't what we were paid for.

first_down.pc: Your friend's done. You can still walk away.

victory.text: Red cord on both their wrists. Covenant money, paid in the Sparrow.

victory.pc: Wendel sent us down here to die. I want to hear him explain it.

defeat.enemy: Take their purses. Leave them for the mere. Wendel owes us a drink.

flee.enemy: That's it, run home! Tell Wendel we said hello!

encounters.name: Up Out of the Water
encounters.description: The water on either side of the causeway stands up, and keeps standing up, and has arms.
encounters.rearm_description: The reeds you cut through have closed again, and the mere on either side of the road is standing up the way it did before. Something has called them back — the same something that rang the bell.

scene.setting: The mere keeps what goes into it. These went in with stones on their ankles, a long time ago, and somebody has asked them back up.
ambiance: Water runs off them in sheets and never stops running.
The reeds close behind you. There is no path now but through.
A stone on a rope drags across the causeway, grinding.

opening.text: They come up out of the water without a ripple, stones still swinging from their ankles, and walk toward you on the bottom of the shallows.

opening.pc: Stay on the causeway. Whatever you do, stay out of the water.

first_down.pc: It went back down. Let it stay there.

victory.text: The water takes them back. The ropes go down last.

victory.pc: Somebody tied those stones on. Somebody in Millhaven.

defeat.text: Cold water closes over your face, and a hand holds you under, patiently, the way it was once held under itself.

flee.pc: North! Get back up the causeway!

flee.text: They wade after you a little way, and then stand in the shallows, watching, water running off them.

encounters.name: The Miller's Welcome
encounters.description: They were sitting in the dark on the far side of the millstone, and they are on their feet the moment your boots touch the dry boards. One of them is still holding a length of the same red cord as the bundle.

scene.setting: The end of the Mere Road. Nobody ever took Elara down here, and the people waiting in the mill have known that all along.
ambiance: The locked wheel creaks against the weed, trying to turn.
Water drips from the millstone dais onto the dry floor, and dries.
The sacking bundle in the corner is exactly the size of a child.

opening.enemy: Didn't think you'd make it past the reeds. Wendel owes me two silver.

opening.pc: Where is the girl?

opening.enemy: Girl? Never was a girl. Just a bundle of sacking and a story for fools.

bloodied.enemy: Get it up out of the water! Get it on them!

first_down.pc: Talk, and you live. Who paid you?

victory.text: The last of them goes into the mere and does not come up.

victory.pc: A decoy. The whole road was a decoy. She was never here.

defeat.enemy: Wrap them in the sacking. Wendel can have them for his next story.

flee.enemy: Go on, then! It's a long road back, and it's filling up behind you.

encounters.name: The Night Patrol
encounters.description: At the end of a row of empty shelves, something in palace armour turns on its heel and begins, without hurrying, to walk towards you.
encounters.rearm_description: There is a suit on patrol between the shelves again — another, or the same one put back together. Someone came down the stair behind you and wound it; the key in its back is still turning.

scene.setting: Under the Grand Library, where the missing books went. The warden was set to walk these stacks before the library had its name, and no one has told it to stop.
ambiance: The key in the warden's back turns, click, click, click.
Empty shelves go back into the dark further than any lamp.
Dust falls from the ceiling at every step the warden takes.

opening.text: The warden stops mid-patrol. The helm turns toward you with a grinding of old iron, and the halberd comes down level.

opening.pc: Get behind it. The key. Somebody get to the key.

bloodied.pc: It is slowing. The key is winding down!

first_down.pc: Down. Pull the key before it gets up.

victory.text: The key stops turning. The armour stands a moment longer on nothing, then comes apart like a dropped tray of cutlery.

victory.pc: Hale knew this was down here. He sent us anyway.

defeat.text: The warden resumes its patrol, stepping over you on the second pass as carefully as it steps over the fallen shelves.

flee.text: It does not follow. Its patrol does not go that way.

encounters.name: The Readers
encounters.description: Two of the skulls in the wall are not set in mortar, and neither are the things behind them. They climb down.
encounters.rearm_description: The skulls you left facing out have all been turned back to the wall, and the two empty niches are not empty any more.

scene.setting: The Readers were archivists once, sent down to catalogue the sealed stacks and kept down here since. They have been fed just enough.
ambiance: Skulls in the wall seem to turn a little further as you pass.
One of the Readers licks ink from its knuckles.
Somewhere below, pages turn in the dark.

opening.enemy: Shh. Quiet in the stacks. Quiet.

opening.pc: You were people. Archivists. Do you remember?

opening.enemy: We remember hunger. Hunger is quieter than you.

bloodied.pc: They feel it. Keep them off the stair!

first_down.enemy: Pell. Pell is gone. More for us.

victory.text: The last one folds over itself on the stair with a sound like a book being closed.

victory.pc: Somebody sent them down here and told their families a story.

defeat.enemy: Quiet now. Quiet. We will catalogue you.

flee.enemy: Come back. Come back when you are hungrier.

encounters.name: The Vault's Keepers
encounters.description: Two figures in crimson rise from where they were kneeling in front of the seal, and a third thing, on a chain, rises with them. They were not praying. They were listening for your feet on the stair.

scene.setting: The seal at the bottom of the stair is painted plaster. Everything about the Under-Archive was a lie to keep you busy, and these are the people told to keep it.
ambiance: Brush strokes show in the painted seal when the light moves.
Up the stair behind you, small sounds, getting closer.
The kneeling mats are still warm.

opening.enemy: You were meant to stay below longer. The Queen will be so disappointed.

opening.pc: The Queen can tell us herself.

opening.enemy: Oh, she will. She always does.

bloodied.enemy: Hold them here! Hold them as long as you can!

first_down.pc: Holding us here for what? What are we missing up there?

victory.text: The satchel by the mats is still open, and there is a letter in it under a black wax seal.

victory.pc: A painted seal. We have been digging in the wrong place.

defeat.enemy: Keep them below. As long as they are willing to stay.

flee.enemy: Run upstairs, then. It is all the same to us. You are late either way.

encounters.name: Still Keeping Watch
encounters.description: In the middle of the oak ring, where no field has ever been, a scarecrow stands with its arms out. It was not here before. Its head turns to follow you.

scene.setting: Marta's scarecrow, walked three fields off its pole into the oak ring the night Elara went, and standing guard over nothing since. Whatever took the girl passed close enough to wake it.
ambiance: Straw sifts out of the old coat with every movement.
A crow lands on an oak branch, looks at the scarecrow, and leaves in a hurry.
Elara's ribbon flutters at its wrist.

opening.text: Its arms come down from their crucifix stretch, slowly, and the turnip head tilts at you, as if you were a crow.

opening.pc: It is only trying to keep the birds off. We are the birds.

first_down.pc: Get the ribbon. Elara will want it back.

victory.text: It goes up like a bonfire, all at once, and the coat last.

victory.pc: Save the ribbon. Leave the rest to burn.

defeat.text: The scarecrow stands over you with its arms out, keeping you from the crows until morning.

flee.text: It does not chase. It goes back to the middle of the ring and puts its arms out again.

encounters.name: The Last Shift
encounters.description: Down past the last lamp, picks are ringing in a steady rhythm, the way they would at the start of a shift. Two figures are working the red face with their backs to you. The tally-tokens on their belts catch the light.

scene.setting: The last shift down the Bloodstone mine: nine men, a token each. The red grain got into them the way it gets into the rock, and they have been working the face ever since.
ambiance: The picks ring on the beat, the way a shift keeps time.
Red light pulses in the veins of the walls, and in theirs.
Somewhere up the shaft, the shift bell rings for nobody.

opening.text: Two of them turn from the face together, on the beat, and bring their picks round.

opening.pc: Brask is waiting for you up top. We are taking you home.

bloodied.text: Red light leaks from the wound instead of blood.

first_down.pc: Get its token. Brask counts every one.

victory.text: The picks stop. For the first time in a month there is silence at the face.

victory.pc: Nine tokens. Brask will want to count them himself.

defeat.text: The shift goes back to the face, and the rhythm picks up where it left off, as if you had never interrupted.

flee.text: Behind you the picks start again, on the beat.

encounters.name: The Gatehouse Watch
encounters.description: Two gate-wardens stand in front of the gatehouse door, not the gate. Behind the door, very quietly, someone is crying, and someone else is telling them to hush.

scene.setting: The gatehouse at Thornhaven holds the families Malachai keeps to buy obedience: servants' children, a clerk's wife, an archivist's daughter. Two wardens stand between them and you.
ambiance: Behind the gatehouse door, somebody is being hushed.
The gravel of the drive has been raked into perfect lines.
Crimson lacquer flakes from the wardens' plate as they move.

opening.enemy: Visiting hours are over. They are always over.

opening.pc: Open that door, and you can walk away.

opening.enemy: We are paid to stand here. We have not been paid to walk.

bloodied.enemy: Hold the door! Whatever happens, hold the door!

first_down.pc: One down. The door is next.

victory.text: Behind the gatehouse door, the hushing stops. Somebody knocks, very quietly, from the inside.

victory.pc: We are here. We are getting you out.

defeat.enemy: Put them in with the others. Vex likes a full house.

flee.enemy: Come back with more friends. The door is not going anywhere.

encounters.name: The Queen's Rearguard
encounters.description: Two figures rise from behind the fallen paving with glaives already levelled. They were left here to see that nobody followed, and they have been looking forward to somebody trying.

scene.setting: The crack the earthquake opened down the middle of Valorheim. The Queen went down it with the last of her faithful, and left two of them at the top so that nobody would follow her.
ambiance: Grit sifts down from the plaza whenever somebody up there walks too near the edge.
The light from above is one blade wide, and the fight keeps drifting out of it.
Somewhere a long way below, something turns over in its sleep.

opening.enemy: The Queen said somebody would come. She did not say it would be you.

opening.pc: Where has she gone?

opening.enemy: Down. Where you are not going.

bloodied.pc: They are faithful, not immortal. Press them!

first_down.text: The zealot goes down with the crimson cord still tight round both wrists.

first_down.pc: Stand aside, and you can still go up.

victory.text: The last zealot lies on the fallen paving, looking down the crack, the way the Queen went.

victory.pc: Down, then. She has a start on us, and she will have used it.

defeat.enemy: Roll them over the edge. Let them go down after all.

flee.pc: Up! Back up into the light!

flee.enemy: Run to your King. Tell him his wife sends her love.

encounters.name: Those Who Chose
encounters.description: Figures come out of the open doorways the way neighbours come out to see who is passing. There is not quite enough of any of them. They come to meet you anyway.

scene.setting: A whole street of the Quiet Kingdom, swept and waiting, and its people still in it, or what is left of them after a thousand years of choosing to stop.
ambiance: A shutter swings open and shut on a breeze that is not blowing.
The bucket on the well chain turns slowly, first one way and then the other.
Every door on the street stands open, and every doorway is dark all the way to the back.

opening.text: They come out of the doorways in silence, soft at the edges, like people remembered by somebody who is forgetting them.

opening.pc: They are not trying to hurt us. They are trying to finish.

bloodied.pc: They come apart when you hit them, like wet paper. Keep on!

first_down.text: The first of them simply stops, and is a little less there, and then not there at all.

first_down.pc: Rest. You have been at it long enough.

victory.text: The street is empty again, swept and ready, with every door open for visitors who are not coming.

victory.pc: A whole city chose this. A whole city.

defeat.text: The last thing you see is a doorway, open and swept, with room inside for one more.

flee.pc: Back up to the rift! Now!

flee.text: They do not follow. They go back into their houses and sit down to wait.

encounters.name: The Litany of Ending
encounters.description: In the bottom of the bowl a figure in colourless vestments is reading aloud, and one of the Unmade kneels in front of it, listening. The reading stops when you come in. The figure turns the page and begins on you.

scene.setting: The temple where the Quiet Kingdom prayed itself to a stop, and the priest who led the prayer, still reading the last page aloud to anyone who will kneel.
ambiance: The litany goes on under everything, a line at a time, even when the Hierophant is not speaking.
The colour is going out of your cloaks, a thread at a time.
The bowl of the floor draws your feet toward the middle, very gently.

opening.enemy: Kneel. There is room. There has always been room.

opening.pc: We are not here to pray.

opening.enemy: Nobody ever is, at first.

bloodied.pc: It is losing its place in the book! Keep at it!

bloodied.enemy: No matter. I know the ending by heart.

first_down.text: The kneeling figure lies down in the bottom of the bowl, as if that were what it had been waiting for.

first_down.pc: That was not rest. That was an ending.

victory.text: The litany stops in the middle of a line, and for the first time in a thousand years the temple is entirely silent.

victory.pc: The stair goes down. So did she.

defeat.enemy: There. Now you are kneeling. Was that so hard?

flee.pc: Out! Out of the bowl, before it takes us!

flee.enemy: Go, then. The litany will keep. It always has.

encounters.name: What the Patrol Found
encounters.description: The floor of the guard post heaves, and heaves again, and the boards go up in splinters round something that is mostly a mouth. It has been waiting under here since the last lot came in. It is hungry again.

scene.setting: The guard post the Third Patrol was keeping, fallen whole into the buried street, and under its floor the thing that ate them.
ambiance: The lamp on its hook swings when the floor heaves, throwing the shadows about.
Somebody's helmet rolls out from under a bench, empty.
Under the boards, stone grinds on stone like a millwheel.

opening.text: The maw comes up through the floor in a burst of splinters, jaws of stone grinding open.

opening.pc: Eight men. It had eight men, and it is still hungry.

bloodied.pc: It is cracking! Keep it up out of its hole!

victory.text: The maw settles into the broken floor and does not move again. Among the stones in its gullet there is a great deal of palace armour.

victory.pc: We will take them home. What there is of them.

defeat.text: The floor closes over you like water, and the grinding starts again.

flee.pc: Out of the post! Into the street!

flee.text: The maw sinks back under the boards to wait, as it waited for the last lot.

encounters.name: The Name-Eater
encounters.description: Out on the causeway something long and pale is bent over the stones, and the scraping sound is its tongue. It lifts its head. It says a name you do not know, and then one you do.

scene.setting: The causeway where the Quiet Kingdom carved the names of everyone it meant to stop, and the servant it left to eat them, still at the work.
ambiance: The scraping of its tongue on the stones never quite stops, even while it fights.
Names you step over are gone when you look back for them.
The dark on either side has no bottom, and nothing comes up out of it: not a sound, not a draught.

opening.enemy: Oswin. Pell. Tessaly. Wenna.

opening.pc: Those are names from the valley. How do you have those?

opening.enemy: Somebody carved them. I eat what is carved.

victory.text: The Name-Eater slides off the edge of the causeway into the dark, and takes nothing with it but itself.

victory.pc: Look. The newest name. Somebody cut it this week.

defeat.enemy: I will eat yours slowly. You will not miss it.

flee.enemy: Go. I have your names now. I have all the time there is.

encounters.name: The Quiet Court in Session
encounters.description: The King on the dais lifts his head for the first time in a thousand years. "Visitors," he says, and down the long approach two of his courtiers turn to face you, drawing thin blades with no hurry at all.

scene.setting: The throne room Valorheim's was copied from, the court still in its places, and the last King of the Quiet waking to find he has company.
ambiance: The courtiers along the approach turn their heads together to follow the fight, like a field of wheat in a wind.
There is no echo in here. Every sound you make simply stops.
The King speaks softly, and you hear every word of it anyway.

opening.enemy: You have come a long way down. Would you like to stop? You may. It is allowed here.

opening.pc: We would like the Queen of Valorheim. Where is she?

opening.enemy: Below, with the thing we could not bring ourselves to use. I am sorry. I shall have to insist.

bloodied.enemy: Ah. It has been so long since anything hurt.

bloodied.pc: He is slowing! Keep at him!

first_down.text: A courtier folds down into its robes at the side of the approach, as neatly as a letter.

victory.text: The last King of the Quiet sits down on the step of his dais, very carefully, lays his sceptre across his knees, and stops.

victory.pc: There is something on the arm of the throne. A tablet.

defeat.enemy: There. Stopping is not so hard. You will see.

flee.enemy: Go if you must. We shall be here. We are always here.

encounters.name: The Last Seal-Breakers
encounters.description: Two masons in Covenant aprons are working the lowest whole seal with chisels, in rhythm, like men setting a millstone. They put down the mallets when they see you. They pick up something heavier.

scene.setting: The shaft of seals the Quiet Kingdom set over its Vessel, and the last of the Covenant's masons, a few blows from breaking the lowest.
ambiance: Chips of red stone rattle down the shaft from the broken seals above.
The lowest seal hums under every blow, like a bell with a cloth over it.
Far below, something breathes out, slow as a tide.

opening.enemy: Three more blows. Three. Could you not have come in an hour?

opening.pc: Put the chisel down, mason.

opening.enemy: I have waited all my life for this seal. I am not putting anything down.

bloodied.pc: They are masons, not soldiers. Keep them off that seal!

first_down.text: A mallet rings on the floor of the well and rolls in a circle before it lies still.

first_down.pc: One left, and he is not finishing that seal.

victory.text: The last chisel rings on the floor of the well. The lowest seal is cracked across, and holding.

victory.pc: Holding. Just. Whatever is under it, she is down there with it.

defeat.enemy: Lie there. You will want to watch this.

flee.enemy: Run. It will find you wherever you run to, soon enough.

encounters.name: The Vessel Wakes
encounters.description: The Queen stands, the chain running from her wrists to the thing in the Cradle, and the thing in the Cradle moves the way a sleeper moves when somebody says its name. "You are just in time," says Liora.

scene.setting: The bottom of everything: the Shadow Vessel dreaming in its cradle, and the Queen of Valorheim chained to it at the wrists, a breath away from climbing in.
ambiance: The Vessel breathes, and every lamp you brought gutters on the out-breath.
The chain between them tightens and slackens, tightens and slackens, like a pulse.
The dark in the Cradle is thicker than dark should be, and it is getting thicker.

opening.enemy: Aldric sent you. Of course he did. He never could do anything himself.

opening.pc: It is over, Liora. The Covenant is finished. Vex is dead.

opening.enemy: Vex was a door. I am the one walking through it.

bloodied.enemy: Careful! Whatever you do to me, you do to it!

bloodied.pc: Then we will be very thorough.

first_down.text: One of them falls, and the chain between them goes slack.

first_down.pc: The chain! Break the chain while it is slack!

victory.text: The Vessel settles back into its cradle, and the chain parts link by link, like a rope of sand. The breathing slows, and slows, and stops being breathing.

victory.pc: It is asleep. Properly asleep. Nobody is climbing into anything today.

defeat.enemy: Hush now. It will all be quiet soon. I promise.

flee.enemy: Run to Aldric. Tell him I shall be home soon, and wearing something new.
